details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1291-1604 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `PREPUSH_TEST_GATE_MODE: ${{ vars.PREPUSH_TEST_GATE_MODE || 'repair' }}` was added only to the "Process each tracking issue" env (line 1294) and not to the "Run standalone stall recovery without active projects" env, so the two env blocks differ and the `PREPUSH_TEST_GATE_MODE=off` kill switch does not reach the recovery sweep.
  WHY: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_workflow_contract.py:356 (`assert sweep_env == full["env"]`) already fails in static-checks on head 910efd4 (run 40396357124), which blocks merge, and the sweep falls back to the script default `repair`; reviewers rated it BLOCKER, and sonnet and minimax also filed the kill-switch bypass on its own as MAJOR.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:4312-4342 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `if:` conditions of "Enable auto-merge on PR" (line 4312) and "Mark linked issues ready to merge" (line 4342) do not include `env.INTEGRATION_TEST_REPAIR_ACTIVE != 'true'`.
  WHY: In a post_sync_test_repair run, "Commit changes" is skipped, so did_commit is empty and both steps fire: auto-merge is enabled and ai:ready-to-merge is applied on a head no reviewer or editor examined, before "Push all pending commits" pushes the repair commit (the PR #2542 stale-head class); all reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1284-1329, 1484-1502 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_resolver_test_repair_context` reads state and fingerprints only from `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V1` comments, but the poller writes `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE_V2`, so fingerprints are stale or `{}`.
  WHY: A `{}` file is 2 bytes, so the fingerprint hard gate is skipped and a repair can revert a merged sub-issue's intent; sonnet rated it NIT because it matches the existing review_conflict_prepare.sh limitation and the agents.d "Known gaps" entry, while the other four rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_prepush_test_gate.sh:97-99, 358-393 (with prompts/integration-sync-test-repair.txt:11-19) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: review_prepush_test_gate_build_prompt prints the captured failures after `=== CAPTURED TEST FAILURES (UNTRUSTED) ===` with no closing END marker, and neutralise() changes only lines that start with `::`, so test output can imitate trusted sections such as `=== EFFECTIVE REPAIR ALLOW-LIST ===`.
  WHY: The allow-list and diff check limit which files change, not the intent of the repair, so a failing test can steer edits inside the allow-list; sonnet rated it NIT and noted that the prompt guard also labels the real allow-list as data, while the other three rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1492-1502 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The integration post-sync test repair prompt (prompts/integration-sync-test-repair.txt) embeds the test failure output directly into the repair prompt without sanitizing it or wrapping it in the required untrusted delimiters.
  WHY: Captured output that mimics prompt section markers or repair task commands can be read by the model as instructions and could override the repair allow-list.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12523-12543, 12855-13360, 24590-24592 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_dispatch_integration_test_repair` increments the shared `.integration_conflict_total_dispatches` on every clean sync or sibling merge, including HTTP 204 "nothing to merge" syncs, but never sets `integration_conflict_episode_base_sha`, so integration_conflict_reset_on_progress never gives those slots back.
  WHY: After INTEGRATION_CONFLICT_LIFETIME_MAX (default 10) routine head changes, the next real conflict goes straight to the lifetime-cap branch at line 12959 and the project is parked for a human without a resolver attempt; repair dispatches also stop permanently (reason=lifetime_cap).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12991-12996 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `_dispatch_integration_test_repair ... || true` call at line 12994, inside the lifetime-cap branch after mark_integration_sync_clean, re-checks the unchanged counter against the same cap and always returns `outcome=skipped reason=lifetime_cap`.
  WHY: The hook placed on the late-mergeable recovery path can never dispatch and only logs a misleading skip; sonnet and minimax rated it NIT, and glm raised it inside its MAJOR shared-counter finding.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:24585-24603 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: After a successful `gh workflow run`, a failure of the `jq ... > "${STATE_FILE}.tmp" && mv` state update is not checked, and a failure of `post_state_comment` only emits a warning, yet the helper still returns success.
  WHY: The next tick reloads the old integration_test_repair_sha and dispatches the same head again, which breaks the one-dispatch-per-head-SHA guarantee and uses up another lifetime-cap slot; sonnet rated it NIT and the other four rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:24585-24603 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: No shared lock protects the STATE_FILE rewrite, so two concurrent poller ticks (a recovery sweep and the full poller) can both pass the SHA dedupe on the same head and both dispatch.
  WHY: `_CONFLICT_DISPATCH_TRACKER` is local to one poller run, so both processes run `gh workflow run` and both increment `.integration_conflict_total_dispatches`, wasting lifetime slots.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:24543-24550 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A failed `git fetch ... || true` is ignored and the head is then read from a possibly stale `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>`.
  WHY: If the stale SHA equals the recorded integration_test_repair_sha, the helper reports `already_dispatched` and skips the newer head without any diagnostic.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:24553-24558 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: When STATE_FILE is corrupt, the helper logs `state_unavailable` and returns 0 without retrying, which silently disables the dedupe and the lifetime-cap check.
  WHY: This is the opposite of the fail-closed intent documented at scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:24551-24552.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_prepush_test_gate.sh:729-750 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Integration mode runs the test gate before the repair but never reruns it after the resolver commits, and the workflow pushes whenever `INTEGRATION_TEST_REPAIRED=true`.
  WHY: A repair that leaves the tests failing is still marked repaired and pushed, whereas review mode reruns the gate after a repair at lines 649-652.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_prepush_test_gate.sh:61-63, 715-732 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In review_prepush_test_gate_integration_main, `status_line="$(review_prepush_test_gate_cmd_gate --phase integration ... 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)"` throws away the stderr diagnostics from review_prepush_test_gate_log (module_absent, mode_invalid, config_invalid, ...).
  WHY: When the gate degrades to skipped or unverified, the log shows no reason, unlike the resolver gate at scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1016-1017, which redirects only stdout.
- changelog.d/8210-prepush-gate-integration-repair.md:13-15 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The table row "New GitHub API reads | 0" is wrong, because `_resolver_test_repair_context` adds three REST reads per repair turn: issues/<n>, `gh api user`, and paginated comments.
  WHY: Operators who budget rate limits from the changelog under-count the repair-side traffic.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1294-1297 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The tracking-issue body is embedded verbatim inside the `=== BEGIN UNTRUSTED TRACKING ISSUE BODY ===` / `=== END UNTRUSTED ... ===` block with no byte cap.
  WHY: A long body, or one that contains crafted `=== END UNTRUSTED ... ===` markers, gives the model a larger untrusted corpus to mine for steering lines.
- scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:130-193, 396, 1547-1553 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The `--test-repair` short-circuit at lines 1547-1553 runs after all the conflict-setup side effects: the classification warning, the helpers loader's `exit 1`, and the EXIT trap installed at line 396.
  WHY: Every repair turn emits a misleading warning, and a missing OPENCODE_HELPERS_PATH can fire the EXIT trap's `_dispatch_integration_judge_now`, contradicting the comment at lines 1542-1544.
- tests/test_review_conflict_resolve_sandbox_only.py:_run_test_repair | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The fixture writes `printf '{}'` (2 bytes) to INTEGRATION_FINGERPRINTS_FILE, so the hard gate at scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:1487 never runs and the `outcome=repair_reverted reason=fingerprints` path is never tested.
  WHY: A regression in verify_integration_fingerprints.py or in the INTEGRATION_BRANCH_NAME wiring would not be caught.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
